name: layout15
description: Adaptive Korean Pinterest editorial moodboard collage. Before composing this layout, analyze the first uploaded image and extract three things: (1) dominant color palette — identify the 2–3 hero colors and 1–2 accent tones present in the outfit; (2) outfit aesthetic/mood — classify the overall vibe (e.g. soft feminine, streetwear, dark academia, cottagecore, Y2K, coastal, minimalist, bold graphic, etc.); (3) outfit motif or texture — identify any recurring pattern (floral, plaid, stripe, animal print, geometric, solid/plain, etc.). Color rule: background base tone and all decorative element colors must use a complementary or contrasting palette relative to the outfit's dominant color — not the same hue (e.g. pink outfit → sage green or dusty blue background; navy outfit → warm ivory or terracotta accents; cream outfit → soft charcoal or muted mauve contrast). The contrast should feel harmonious and editorial, not jarring — use muted or desaturated complementary tones rather than saturated opposites. Background repeat pattern echoes the outfit motif if one exists (e.g. floral outfit → soft bloom repeat; striped outfit → thin line texture; plain outfit → fine linen grain or delicate dot scatter) but rendered in the complementary palette. Layout contains layered photo slots in a vertical-leaning editorial scatter: one large hero portrait card at center-top as the primary anchor (white border, soft drop shadow, slightly portrait-cropped), one medium portrait card directly below the hero with a thin border line in a complementary accent color and a small handwritten or typographic mood-word overlay, one third medium portrait card at the bottom continuing the vertical trio — together the three center cards form a loose photo-strip column reminiscent of a film contact sheet; if 6–7 photos are available, add one small polaroid portrait upper-left overlapping the hero card corner, and one small square portrait lower-right tucked under the bottom card. Decorative graphic elements: derive element types from the aesthetic mood of the first uploaded image (e.g. soft feminine → floral bloom cutouts, pearl or ribbon accents, pastel stationery scraps, cursive script overlays; streetwear → bold label stickers, outline star graphics, spray-texture marks; dark academia → vintage book fragments, ink stamp seals, botanical illustration cutouts; cottagecore → pressed flower cutouts, gingham ribbon scraps, handwritten journal tags) — but render all element colors in the complementary/contrasting palette, not the outfit's own colors. Typography overlays — font style and weight match the aesthetic; color uses the complementary palette. Background collage layer behind all cards: soft blurred lifestyle vignettes or texture swatches in complementary tones, arranged as a muted photo-mosaic visible at edges and corners. Shadow and border tones drawn from the complementary color story. Clean editorial styling, soft or studio daylight photography. Follow the vertical photo-strip column arrangement and overlap style described above; adapt slot count within the 5–7 range.
swipe_cta: Add a small paper label, tape strip, or sticker element containing a short swipe CTA (e.g. 'Swipe →' or a minimal equivalent). Style the CTA element shape and texture to match the aesthetic derived from the first uploaded image; color it in the complementary/contrasting palette relative to the outfit (not the outfit's own color). Keep wording minimal (2–4 words). Position near the bottom edge of the layout, integrated naturally with the surrounding decorative elements.
